subject: Clarify counting CDN-origin failover in uptime ledger
messages:
From: OrbitNet SRE <sre@orbitnet.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>; Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>; Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected failover at edge-cdn-3 — request for SLA accounting

Hi team,

Quick note from OrbitNet SRE: on 2027-04-28 22:37:00 UTC our edge-cdn-3 node observed an origin connection failure that triggered an automated failover to secondary edge cluster. Customer traffic to your account (acme-retail) dropped by ~17% for 21 minutes while clients retried.

We believe the full 21-minute interval should be counted against Redwood's availability ledger for the affected region — the failover was observed at the CDN layer but downstream requests were returning 503/timeout from our vantage. Please see the attached incident timeline (orbitnet-incident-timeline.pdf) and preliminary packet capture excerpts.

Can you confirm how Redwood will account for this interval? OrbitNet is preparing a partial-credits request and would like to avoid a prolonged dispute.

Thanks,
Amit Shah
SRE Lead, OrbitNet
Attachment: orbitnet-incident-timeline.pdf

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <sre@orbitnet.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected failover at edge-cdn-3 — request for SLA accounting

Amit — thanks for the quick heads up and for the timeline. We looked at our top-level metrics and saw a corresponding spike in 5xxs from the edge during that window but we also have a series of probe timeouts that overlap the same period.

To speed this up: can you confirm whether the client traffic drop you saw was broadly cross-customer (affecting multiple customers on that edge) or specific to traffic routed to our origin? That will help us decide if this falls under a third-party exclusion or something we need to credit.

I'll loop in our infra lead (Connor) for the probe-level artifacts — happy to set a quick 30-min call if that helps.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <sre@orbitnet.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected failover at edge-cdn-3 — request for SLA accounting

Amit / team — digging into probe logs (attached: redwood-probe-logs-20270429.zip). Quick summary:
- Our synthetic probes to the affected prefix started failing at 2027-04-28T22:36:42Z.
- At 22:40:10Z we observed partial degradation: client requests were getting 5xx errors but some requests succeeded (long tail latency).
- At 22:45:05Z we started routing to a cached fallback (TTL-based) for a subset of routes; that reduced error rate but introduced stale-response risks for live inference calls.
- Full recovery (origin routing restored and cache invalidation completed) was at 22:58:23Z.

Per our SLA terms, we typically exclude provider-originated maintenance/failures when the root cause is a third-party CDN control plane action; however, if downstream customer requests are failing (not just being routed to a cached response) we treat that as partial degradation and compute credit proportionally.

Proposed approach: apportion the 21-minute window into 3 segments — initial failover (first ~4 minutes) where CDN control-plane initiated failover (exclude), middle partial-degrade window (minutes 5–14) compute partial-credit using error-rate weighting, final minutes (15–21) count as full customer-impact window. Details in attached spreadsheet (proposed-apportionment-formula.xlsx).

Open to discussing — happy to hop on the call if needed.

—Connor
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-probe-logs-20270429.zip

From: Alicia Mendez <alicia@orbitnet.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@orbitnet.com
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected failover at edge-cdn-3 — request for SLA accounting

Evelyn / Connor — thanks for the quick analysis. OrbitNet's point: our telemetry shows the user request drop was customer-visible and cross-tenant on that edge. From a commercial standpoint OrbitNet believes the entire 21 minutes should be eligible for credit since failover was initiated by our CDN's origin connector and Redwood's origin endpoints were the downstream dependency for our routing decisions.

We reviewed Redwood's proposed apportionment and can't accept selective exclusion without a mutual definition of "cache-protected" traffic. For our contention: customers retried and saw degraded UX; whether the cache served stale data or 503s, the observable impact is what matters for credits.

Please advise next steps — if we can't reach a quick agreement we'd like to escalate to account management (Laura) and Legal to preserve options for a formal claim.

Alicia Mendez
Senior Counsel, OrbitNet
Attachment: none
Related link: https://docusign.com/Envelope/ABC-123-ORB

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Mendez <alicia@orbitnet.com>, Amit Shah <sre@orbitnet.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, legal@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 May 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected failover at edge-cdn-3 — request for SLA accounting

Alicia / OrbitNet team — thanks for the clarity. We're committed to resolving this quickly. Internal recap: we have probe artifacts that show a layered event (control-plane failover followed by partial degrade and then cache-assisted mitigation). To avoid prolonged disputes we propose the following compromise for this single event:

1) Exclude first 3 minutes from credits if the CDN control-plane triggered an immediate failover (our logs show control-plane event at 22:36:40Z).
2) Treat minutes 4–14 as partial-degrade and calculate a proportional credit using Redwood's error-rate weighting (formula attached).
3) Treat minutes 15–21 as full-impact for credit purposes.

We will apply the above to the incident for Acme-Retail and post the resulting ledger entry in the account's availability report by EOD May 4, 2027. If OrbitNet provides an independent traffic-sampling export to verify the cross-tenant impact (CSV or s3), we can include that in the reconciliation.

Next steps / action items:
- OrbitNet: share customer traffic-sampling export (requested format: CSV, s3 link) by May 4.
- Redwood (Connor): post apportionment calculation and raw probe artifacts to shared Drive by EOD May 3.
- Laura Bennett will prepare a short mutual action note for account teams.

If that works for you we'll treat this as a one-off and avoid adjustments to the broader SLA language for now. If not, we can open a formal claim channel.

Thanks — looking forward to the data so we can reconcile quickly.

Karthik Iyer
VP, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-apportionment-formula.xlsx
